title: Constructive conditions of exchange
summary: A constructive condition is a dependency the law recognizes between the parties’ performances even when the agreement does not expressly use conditional language.
notes:
Kingston shows the significance of the order of performance: provision of security was required before the other party had to turn over the business. More generally, an exchange may require simultaneous performance or performance by one side before the other must act. A breach does not automatically excuse every remaining duty; its materiality and the governing dependency matter.

Substantial-performance and divisibility doctrines can soften the consequences of incomplete performance. Jacob & Youngs distinguishes a minor, innocent departure in construction from a failure that defeats the exchange. Identify whether the disputed condition is express or supplied by law, because the governing degree of required compliance may differ.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.constructive-conditions: The law can make one performance a prerequisite to the other.
